Solberg was born on July 25, 1895, in Kristiania, Norway (now Oslo). He developed an interest in meteorology at an early age and pursued his passion by studying physics and mathematics at the University of Oslo. He earned his Ph.D. in 1924 with a dissertation on atmospheric electricity. Career

Solberg's academic career spanned over four decades, during which he held various positions at the University of Oslo, including professor of meteorology from 1936 to 1965. He was also the director of the Norwegian Meteorological Institute from 1946 to 1965. Contributions to Meteorology

Solberg's research focused on atmospheric electricity, weather forecasting, and the application of mathematical methods to meteorology. He developed a new method for forecasting weather patterns using atmospheric pressure and temperature data, which became widely used in Norway and other European countries. Nobel Prize Nomination

Halvor Solberg was nominated for the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1934 for his groundbreaking work on atmospheric electricity and its application to weather forecasting.
